This binding may alter the function of Slc6a2, potentially affecting neurotransmitter homeostasis. The evidence indicates that Doxepin indirectly influences Slc6a2 through its effects on Methylphenidate, which in turn modulates Slc6a2 activity. The mechanism involves a cascade where Doxepin's effects on the nervous system trigger a chain of molecular interactions, ultimately impacting Slc6a2. The strength of this relationship is supported by the scores and the hierarchical connections in the network, though the exact nature of the interaction between Doxepin and Methylphenidate remains partially understood.
